mathematical_decisions.argument: All stated n>=10, s,t>=2, s+t<=n-1 satisfy UA.Edge with the affine base of order 2^(delta+5), delta=n-1-s-t. The two dihedral maps are faithful on proper marked subgroups, their supports are incomparable, and the order exponent is delta+5+(s-2)+(t-2)=n. Pair orders and all marked intersections are inherited from the proved construction. This proves existence, not uniqueness or the source-specific presentation used in its original existence proof.

The even-word subgroup has index two by the actual Frattini basis. The retained cyclic-core inequality gives the explicitly sized cyclic subgroup A, characteristic in the core and hence normal in the even subgroup; b inverts it. Original end intersection gives quotient IP and the exact bounded type. The three binary groups D and automorphisms T are explicitly defined; the bilinear multiplication proves the last group has sixteen elements. The central product with C_m retains both factors, and the stated A,C maps preserve the defining relations, are commuting involutions, and give the correct pair orders and rank-three IP. The eight invariant words distinguish the ordered markings. The converses separately handle the two easy bounded quotients and the four genuinely exhaustive order-256 seeds; the two excluded seeds cannot lift for m>=32, and the surviving commutator relations force the displayed models. Finally the bare presentations are bounded independently before identifying their finite images. Thus no finite image is mistaken for an upper bound, and no finite sample is extrapolated to all n. The s=5 estimate uses the actual affine quotient W/4Z^2, of order128.

The principal equivalence is the source equivalence on distinguished generator sets. For a connected string diagram it is exactly preservation or reversal of the ordered marking, not arbitrary abstract group isomorphism. The endpoint rotation cosets are distinct by original IP, giving 2 times the adjacent-order product and the rank-five bound at order1024. Disconnected strings split by actual commuting subgroups and IP. The smooth Coxeter epimorphism and Frattini characters are explicit. Every retained low-rank intersection criterion includes its full hypotheses. The two quotient criteria use the actual quotient marking, with both the no-end-product-kernel case and the kernel-contained-in-one-end case checked.

The central end-product lemma starts from the unique rotation-coset expression. Commutation with b restricts the rotation exponent; the remaining dihedral centralizer gives exactly the printed candidates. If xy is central then x and y separately are. The possible ybx is ruled out by the original Frattini basis: a,ybx,c would be three commuting involutions generating a group with an adjacent product of order at least4. A central half-rotation gives a quotient with one adjacent order halved; otherwise a central involution lies outside the end product and preserves both ends. The continuation through degenerate intermediate markings is explicit and stops at C2^3. The source Corollary3.7 does not literally hold at order8; the correction is necessary and stated.

For an actual central extension by C2 with the marked lifts involutory and distant markers commuting, both adjacent orders cannot double, because the same central involution would belong to both end rotations and contradict IP. Each defining relator of a complete quotient presentation lifts to its actual value 1 or z. The proposed presentation maps onto G and has order at most twice the quotient order, proving completeness. At least one relation detects z. The three patterns classify successful lifts only; arbitrary binary assignments still require exact order and IP checks.

mathematical_decisions.decision: accepted conditional on the explicitly retained exact algorithms
mathematical_decisions.argument: UA.Search supplies the universal nilpotent bound, the canonical gamma3 quotient and exhaustive invariant subgroup ladder for each of the four (rank,excess) pairs. The implementation transports the original involutions through NQ and the pc isomorphism. Every normal index-two child comes from a hyperplane of M/[M,U]Phi(M); all hyperplanes are checked, and only equal actual canonical subgroup keys are deduplicated. All subset intersections are evaluated for every final candidate, including candidates failing the earlier kernel-profile test. Counts are compared after generation and never filter candidates. Reversal is the actual automorphism of the universal group and acts on its normal kernels. The rank/order bound exhausts every nondegenerate rank at order1024. This is a finite proof conditional on GAP/NQ algorithms, not a Lean theorem.

All four printed order512 bases, all twelve binary assignments, both ClassII groups and every literal Table4 row are evaluated as full presentations. The central quotient of each lift is matched to the named base with the generators fixed. The eight intended classes are pairwise distinct and bijectively match the independent full rank-three census. The literal printed label map (a,b,c,d,e,f,g,h)->(a,b,c,d,c,a,g,c) is kept separate from the corrected target labels. Changing the second right-hand side in rows e,f,h to tau is the stated repair, with no claim of unique editorial intent or historical priority.

Completed trivial-subgroup Todd-Coxeter computations bound the raw universal presentations. The realized permutation group is checked to have the same order, to satisfy every relator, to be generated by the marked involutions, and to satisfy every subset intersection. The three source examples have exact orders512,1024,2048 and their specified marked ends. All three central involutions of the order2048 group are enumerated, so the order1024 quotient list is exhaustive; exactly two retain type4,4,8 and are distinct with the generators fixed. The remaining quotient has type4,4,4. The geometric universal interpretation remains a stated classical input.

mathematical_decisions.decision: accepted with the stated retained classification
mathematical_decisions.argument: Only the finite smooth square classification is borrowed. The source factor pairing is independently corrected using actual reflection axes, and UA.SquareDecomposition supplies the full group structure including s=1. The change of coordinates from UA.Affine is explicit. In the center proof, commuting with translations forces the linear part to act trivially on the quotient lattice; the faithful-action cases and both small exceptional actions are handled separately. The three listed generators for the smallest diagonal center are explicitly not independent. No first-square-family m=0 center claim is invented.

mathematical_decisions.decision: accepted with the exact infinite decomposition retained
mathematical_decisions.argument: The explicitly marked infinite universal decomposition is attributed to N009 Theorem5.3 and its McMullen-Schulte input. It is not inferred from a stalled coset enumeration. The b,d Frattini characters locate every finite C-quotient kernel in W1 times W2, and also retain the complement, proving the semidirect quotient description. At order1024 the complete census contains exactly two markings with the prescribed unequal ends, and the two literal source presentations are explicitly isomorphic to them. Unequal end orders prevent reversal merging. This replaces the local source case analysis without assuming the completeness of its two presentations.

All107 source rows remain, including the infinite row. Independent extraction of the primary PDF matches all rows, except exactly the four declared right-end orientation corrections in rows63-66. All72 defining Atlas presentations were independently parsed from the already captured primary HTML, with their exact hashes, and agree word-for-word with the data. Every named end is identified by a generator-preserving isomorphism; duals are computed rather than guessed from suffixes. Counts are obtained from the full census, and all106 finite universal orders and their exact ends are checked from complete presentations.
